title: Hierarchical Ti3C2T@MoS2 heterostructures: A first principles calculation and application in corrosion/wear protection
notes: Spine: need -> hypothesis -> (DFT branch: DFT-D method -> imposed registries I-VI -> EB ranking OH >> F > O, charge-redistribution MEC) and (experimental branch: filler modification + loading sweep -> hydrothermal MoS2 growth on f-Ti3C2Tx -> epoxy coating on Q345 -> hierarchical shape, MoS2 identity, agglomeration at 0.5 wt% (argued) -> barrier value and wear-rate value -> 9-d NaCl service) -> conclusion. The DFT branch joins the wear branch at the interlayer-sliding MEC n16, which the paper grounds in the weak O/F interfaces. Audits: o1 (strong OH interface qualifies the sliding MEC), o10 (Ti3C2Tx (002) absent in composite XRD). Figure-vs-text conflicts kept in image_note: EP wear rate 0.7 (text) vs ~0.18 (F10a); EP Rc 7.66e6 (text) vs ~7.6e5 (F9b); wear-width claim not visible in F10b. F3, F4, F6 are tier C (no panels offered): cited with panel_ids []. All offered crops carry no OCR cue classes, so no technique check applies.
